items.basis: The proposed CNN-BiLSTM network with SCSSA optimization is a black box approach that provides no physical insight into the thermal deformation mechanics, making it impossible to validate or debug when real-world conditions deviate from training data.

The candidate fails to specify boundary conditions for different materials, spindle speeds, or cooling systems, yet thermal behavior varies significantly across these parameters as shown in [doi:10.1016/j.aasri.2012.06.032].

The candidate references evidence on thermal analysis for machining centers but provides no evidence that CNN-BiLSTM networks can achieve the required 10-micrometer precision in real-time thermal compensation.

The candidate claims to maintain tool center point within 10 micrometers but provides no comparative data against existing thermal compensation methods that already achieve similar or better results through direct physical modeling.

The proposed system would require real-time thermal data acquisition and processing at microsecond timescales to be effective, which is computationally infeasible with a CNN-BiLSTM architecture as evidenced by the processing requirements in [doi:10.1038/s41598-025-27599-1].

The testable prediction only measures tool center point displacement without isolating the thermal compensation effect from other sources of error such as mechanical vibration or environmental factors.
